accepted.s: The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act was enacted in which year?
accepted.x: The Forty-fourth Amendment was enacted in 1978 by the Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year rather than the misleading figure 1944.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Forty-fourth Constitutional Amendment replaced the expression ‘internal disturbance’ with which expression as a ground for National Emergency?
accepted.x: The Forty-fourth Amendment substituted ‘armed rebellion’ for ‘internal disturbance’ in relation to a National Emergency.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the former and substituted constitutional expressions.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the safeguards introduced by the Forty-fourth Amendment:
1. A National Emergency can be proclaimed only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet.
2. Parliamentary approval must be obtained within one month by a special majority in each House.
3. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Amendment required written Cabinet advice, approval within one month by special majority, and protected Articles 20 and 21 from suspension.
accepted.tq: Check each emergency safeguard separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who can disapprove or revoke a Proclamation of Emergency under the safeguard associated with the Forty-fourth Amendment?
accepted.x: The Forty-fourth Amendment strengthened the power of the Lok Sabha to disapprove or revoke a Proclamation of Emergency.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution specifically empowered to check executive continuation of Emergency.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the right to property after the Forty-fourth Amendment, which one of the following is correct?
o: It remains a Fundamental Right under Article 31.
It became a legal right under Article 300A.
It was made a Directive Principle under Article 39.
It was abolished completely from the Constitution.
accepted.x: Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 were deleted, and the right to property was retained as a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.
accepted.tq: Separate Fundamental Rights from legal rights by checking the Article number.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Articles relating to the right to property were deleted by the Forty-fourth Amendment?
accepted.x: The Amendment deleted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 from the Fundamental Rights chapter.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with the exact constitutional provisions affected.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Forty-fourth Amendment restored the power of courts to hear election disputes relating to which set of offices?
o: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
President, Governor, Prime Minister and Chief Justice of India
Vice-President, Chief Minister, Speaker and Attorney-General
President, Vice-President, Governors and Chief Ministers
accepted.x: It reversed the bar created by the Thirty-ninth Amendment and restored judicial consideration of election disputes concerning the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker.
accepted.tq: Use the office-combination to distinguish the Forty-fourth Amendment from the Thirty-ninth Amendment.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a corrective feature of the Forty-fourth Amendment?
o: It suspended judicial review during Emergency.
It extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies to six years.
It abolished the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution.
It restored the five-year term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies and judicial review.
accepted.x: The Amendment restored the normal five-year term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies and restored judicial review, correcting features of the Thirty-eighth, Thirty-ninth and Forty-second Amendments.
accepted.tq: Find the option that combines the two corrective measures actually associated with the Amendment.
accepted.sec: 44th Amendment - emergency safeguards, property, enacting government  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Constitutional Amendments in chronological order:
A. Forty-second Amendment
B. First Amendment
C. Eighty-sixth Amendment
D. Fifty-second Amendment
accepted.x: The correct sequence is First Amendment (1951), Forty-second (1976), Fifty-second (1985) and Eighty-sixth (2002).
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest amendment years.
accepted.sec: Amendment → year of enactment and chronological order (1st, 42nd, 52nd, 86th, 96th)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sequence of the First, Forty-second, Fifty-second, Eighty-sixth and Ninety-sixth Amendments with their years?
accepted.x: The years are 1951, 1976, 1985, 2002 and 2011 respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each amendment number with its exact enactment year.
accepted.sec: Amendment → year of enactment and chronological order (1st, 42nd, 52nd, 86th, 96th)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ninety-sixth Constitutional Amendment changed the name ‘Oriya’ to which name?
accepted.x: The Ninety-sixth Amendment, enacted in 2011, changed the constitutional reference from ‘Oriya’ to ‘Odia’.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official word in a look-alike language-name pair.
accepted.sec: Amendment → year of enactment and chronological order (1st, 42nd, 52nd, 86th, 96th)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Constitutional Amendment was enacted by which body?
o: A joint sitting of Parliament and State Legislatures
accepted.x: The First Amendment was enacted in 1951 by the Provisional Parliament.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Provisional Parliament from the first elected Parliament.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the Prime Minister when the First Constitutional Amendment was enacted?
accepted.x: The First Amendment was enacted by the Provisional Parliament during the Prime Ministership of Jawaharlal Nehru.
accepted.tq: Separate the political executive from the President who gave assent.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Constitutional Amendment received the assent of President Rajendra Prasad on:
accepted.x: President Rajendra Prasad gave assent to the First Amendment on 18 June 1951.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise day and month associated with the Amendment’s assent.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups of provisions was inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The First Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and added the Ninth Schedule to protect specified land reform laws.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with its distinctive cluster of Articles and Schedule.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision associated with the First Constitutional Amendment?
o: Reservation of one-third seats for women in State Assemblies
accepted.x: Reservation of one-third seats for women in State Assemblies is associated with the 106th Amendment, not the First Amendment. The First Amendment dealt with Article 15(4), Article 19(2), and the Ninth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Eliminate provisions belonging to later amendments and retain the First Amendment cluster.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Amendment inserted Article 15(4) primarily to enable special provisions for:
o: Government servants belonging to SCs only
accepted.x: Article 15(4), inserted by the First Amendment, permits special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and for SCs and STs.
accepted.tq: Identify the beneficiary group rather than confusing Article 15(4) with political reservation.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following cases concerning freedom of speech was overcome by the First Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The First Amendment responded, among other rulings, to Romesh Thappar (1950) on freedom of speech by expanding the permissible grounds for restriction.
accepted.tq: Link the case to the subject matter—speech, land reform or backward-class provisions.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Amendment was enacted, among other reasons, to overcome the effect of which case on reservation for backward classes?
accepted.x: The Champakam Dorairajan judgment led to the insertion of Article 15(4) through the First Amendment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the case connected with Article 15(4) from cases on land reform and amendment power.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which case relating to zamindari abolition was among the judicial rulings addressed by the First Amendment?
o: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
Champakam Dorairajan v. State of Madras
Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar
Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
accepted.x: Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar concerned land reform and zamindari abolition and was among the rulings addressed by the First Amendment.
accepted.tq: Associate the case with land reform rather than speech or backward-class reservation.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The constitutional validity of the First Amendment was upheld in which case?
accepted.x: The First Amendment was upheld by the Supreme Court in Shankari Prasad (1951).
accepted.tq: Use the case connected with the early judicial recognition of Parliament’s amending power.
accepted.sec: 1st Amendment - Ninth Schedule, rulings it overcame, Prime Minister, other provisions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Amendment)
 a. 13th
 b. 35th
 c. 36th
 d. 55th
List-II (Provision or status)
 i. Arunachal Pradesh statehood-related provision
 ii. Nagaland and Article 371A
 iii. Sikkim as an associate State
 iv. Sikkim as a full State
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The 13th Amendment relates to Nagaland, the 35th to Sikkim as an associate State, the 36th to Sikkim as a full State, and the 55th to Arunachal Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Nagaland and Sikkim pairs, then complete the code.
accepted.sec: Statehood and integration → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Sikkim became a full State of the Indian Union under which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Thirty-sixth Amendment of 1975 made Sikkim a full State and omitted Article 2A and the related Tenth Schedule provisions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Sikkim’s associate-State status under the 35th Amendment from full statehood under the 36th.
accepted.sec: Statehood and integration → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment made Sikkim an associate State in 1974?
accepted.x: The Thirty-fifth Amendment of 1974 introduced Sikkim’s associate-State status through Article 2A and a related Tenth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Separate the two successive Sikkim amendments by status and year.
accepted.sec: Statehood and integration → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Goa became a State of India under which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Fifty-sixth Amendment of 1987 dealt with Goa’s statehood and inserted Article 371I.
accepted.tq: Match the statehood event with the adjacent amendment numbers without confusing Goa with Arunachal Pradesh.
accepted.sec: Statehood and integration → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Fifty-third Amendment of 1986 dealt with Mizoram statehood. The Fifty-fifth concerned Arunachal Pradesh and the Fifty-sixth concerned Goa.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched state and amendment after checking the neighbouring statehood entries.
accepted.sec: Statehood and integration → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the successive extensions of SC/ST reservation in legislatures under Article 334?
accepted.x: The listed extensions were made through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended the reservation up to 2030.
accepted.tq: Track the reservation-extension series separately from promotion and service-related amendments.
accepted.sec: SC/ST reservation changes → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 16(4A) relating to reservation in promotion for SCs and STs?
accepted.x: The Seventy-seventh Amendment of 1995 inserted Article 16(4A) concerning reservation in promotion for SCs and STs.
accepted.tq: Associate the Article number with the specific service-reservation amendment.
accepted.sec: SC/ST reservation changes → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The provision allowing backlog vacancies to be treated outside the fifty per cent ceiling was introduced by the:
accepted.x: The Eighty-first Amendment of 2000 inserted Article 16(4B), dealing with backlog vacancies outside the fifty per cent ceiling.
accepted.tq: Match the numerical ceiling clue with Article 16(4B) and the 81st Amendment.
accepted.sec: SC/ST reservation changes → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Relaxation of qualifying marks for SCs and STs in the context of Article 335 was provided by the:
accepted.x: The Eighty-second Amendment of 2000 added a proviso to Article 335 concerning relaxation of qualifying marks and standards for SCs and STs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish qualifying-mark relaxation from backlog vacancies and consequential seniority.
accepted.sec: SC/ST reservation changes → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Consequential seniority in promotions for SCs and STs is associated with which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Eighty-fifth Amendment of 2001 provided for consequential seniority in the context of reservation in promotion.
accepted.tq: Use the service-law phrase ‘consequential seniority’ as the identifying clue.
accepted.sec: SC/ST reservation changes → amendment number  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Articles 371D and 371E relating to Andhra Pradesh were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Thirty-second Amendment of 1973 gave effect to the Six-Point Formula and inserted Articles 371D and 371E.
accepted.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect 33rd Amendment and recall the exact amendment number.
accepted.sec: AP-related Articles 371D and 371E → inserting amendment and subject

accepted.s: Article 371D primarily deals with which of the following in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Regional equity in public employment and education and an Administrative Tribunal
Reservation of women in the State Assembly
Establishment of a Central University only
accepted.x: Article 371D provides for regional equity in public employment and education and provides for an Administrative Tribunal in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the subject from the operational features rather than the Article number alone.
accepted.sec: AP-related Articles 371D and 371E → inserting amendment and subject

accepted.s: Article 371E provides for:
o: An Administrative Tribunal in Andhra Pradesh
A separate High Court for Rayalaseema
A Central University in Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Article 371E enables the establishment of a Central University in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Separate the institutional subject of Article 371E from the regional-equity provisions of Article 371D.
accepted.sec: AP-related Articles 371D and 371E → inserting amendment and subject

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 106th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It received Presidential assent in 2023.
2. It reserves one-third of the seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly.
3. It inserted Articles 330A, 332A and 334A and amended Article 239AA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 106th Amendment received assent in 2023, provided one-third reservation, inserted Articles 330A, 332A and 334A, and amended Article 239AA.
accepted.tq: Verify the year, scope and constitutional Articles before choosing the combined option.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment (2023) - women's reservation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 was preceded as a Bill by which numbered Constitutional Amendment Bill?
accepted.x: The legislation that became the 106th Amendment was introduced as the 128th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the enacted Amendment number from the Bill number.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment (2023) - women's reservation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Implementation of the women’s reservation under the 106th Amendment is linked to delimitation based on:
o: The first Census conducted after the Act, namely the 2027 Census
accepted.x: The reservation is to commence only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, identified in the material as the 2027 Census.
accepted.tq: Connect commencement with the specified future Census and delimitation condition.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment (2023) - women's reservation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For what initial period is the reservation of seats for women under the 106th Amendment provided, subject to extension by Parliament?
accepted.x: The reservation is provided for an initial period of fifteen years and may be extended by Parliament.
accepted.tq: Use the duration figure as the decisive clue and distinguish it from the delimitation date.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment (2023) - women's reservation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the 106th Constitutional Amendment is NOT correct?
o: It came into operation immediately upon assent without any delimitation condition.
It covers the Delhi Legislative Assembly through an amendment to Article 239AA.
accepted.x: The Amendment does not operate immediately upon assent; commencement depends on delimitation based on the first Census after the Act. The other three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Identify the false immediate-effect claim by checking the commencement condition.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment (2023) - women's reservation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
